clue.text: Postpone work on repellent

definitions.meaning: to shelve a project or put a ship or factory into storage for later use
a ball of camphor or naphthalene kept in wardrobes to drive away clothes moths

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: the verb means to shelve a project, and the noun is the little ball that repels moths.

clue.text: Sketch reveals unconscious stuff

parts.note: someone knocked out cold is out
to stuff or fill the inside of something, as in lining one's pockets, is to line it

explanation.surface: A drawing seems to expose material from the subconscious mind.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough drawing showing only the main shape or plan is a synonym for a sketch.

clue.text: Uncompromising firm sound as a bell after strike

indicators.note: after places the bell sound behind the word for strike

parts.note: firm means hard, solid
to strike is to hit
a ting is the clear ringing sound a small bell makes

explanation.surface: A tough company, as sound as a bell, comes out of an industrial strike unbowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound as a bell' looks like the idiom for healthy, but here it is the noise a bell makes.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a forceful, uncompromising report or attack is described as hard-hitting.

clue.text: Started in America by Bush

parts.note: a rose is a flowering bush

explanation.surface: Something began in the US under President Bush.
explanation.walkthrough: Bush looks like the president, but it is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: to have arisen or got up is to have started, as a dispute that started or began.

clue.text: Country doctor? He's too liberal

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as its letters H, E, S
taken as written

explanation.surface: Asked if he is a country doctor, someone replies he is too much of a liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doctor?' looks like the noun after Country, but it is a verb signalling the anagram of HESTOO into ESOTHO, after L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lesotho is a kingdom in southern Africa, entirely surrounded by South Africa, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Deeply affected by fight on street

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the word for fight after the street abbreviation

parts.note: a ruck is a scuffle or brawl

explanation.surface: Someone is moved after witnessing a brawl in the road.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to be struck by something is to be deeply impressed or moved by it.

clue.text: Flute going in Carol's economising

indicators.note: going in means the word for flute is put inside the word for carol

parts.note: to carol is to sing
to flute is to make grooves or folds, as a crimp makes in pastry or hair

explanation.surface: A flautist playing along to Carol's song is cutting costs.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after Carol stands for 'is', a link word. Flute looks like the instrument but is the verb for crimping.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: scrimping is skimping, saving money by spending as little as possible.

clue.text: Crack finally given up by flier

indicators.note: finally given up means the last letter of the word for crack is dropped

parts.note: crack cocaine is known as rock

explanation.surface: A crack addict finally kicks the habit, thanks to someone who flies.
explanation.definitionFit: The roc is a giant bird of Arabian legend, so an example of a flying creature.

clue.text: Joy and Simon — odd ones out for so long

parts.note: cheer is joy or gladness

indicators.note: odd ones out means the odd-numbered letters of the name are removed, leaving the even ones

explanation.surface: Two people, Joy and Simon, seem to be the misfits who stayed away so long.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking out S, M and N (first, third, fifth) from SIMON leaves IO.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British farewells, so a cheery goodbye is a synonym for so long.

clue.text: Tearaway's hoax has Rene edging away extremely frightened

parts.note: a tearaway is an unruly youngster, a terror; with 's it gives the plural form
a hoax is a trick

indicators.note: edging away means the outer letters of the name are dropped, leaving its centre

explanation.surface: A young hooligan's prank leaves Rene sidling off in fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: someone panic-stricken or terrified with fear is extremely frightened.

clue.text: The woman hiding one shilling in well is most odd

indicators.note: in means those letters go inside the word for well

parts.note: well means fit, in good health

indicators.note: hiding means the woman's word wraps around the letter for one

parts.note: the woman is she
one is the Roman numeral I
S is the abbreviation for the old British coin the shilling

explanation.surface: A woman conceals a coin down a well, which is very strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well' looks like a hole for water, but it is the adjective meaning healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Fishy is informal for suspicious or dubious, so the superlative is a synonym for most odd.

clue.text: Poor Georgia reversed into lake

indicators.note: into means that reversed piece goes inside the word for lake

parts.note: a mere is a small lake

indicators.note: reversed means the state abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: GA is the US postal abbreviation for Georgia

explanation.surface: An unlucky Georgian backs into a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a meagre portion is scanty, a poor one.

clue.text: Do in Staines ruined after Wally takes first of amphetamines

indicators.note: after means the rearranged town comes behind the fool and the letter

parts.note: a wally is British slang for a fool, an ass

indicators.note: first of means only the opening letter of the drug word is taken
ruined means the letters of the town are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: Staines is wrecked after an idiot takes speed.
explanation.walkthrough: STAINES is a town near London; 'ruined' rearranges it into SSINATE. 'takes' joins the fool and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Do in is slang for kill, and killing a prominent person is a specific form of it.

clue.text: Move very quickly to a higher position but be quiet

definitions.note: a rude British order to shut up

parts.note: to belt along is to move at great speed
up means to a higher position

explanation.surface: Someone races upstairs but is told to keep the noise down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link word; the definition is British slang for shut up.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: the phrase is a rude British order to shut up and stop talking.

clue.text: Most important scientific law by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the answer is pronounced like the word for a law

parts.note: a principle is a fundamental law in science, such as Archimedes' principle

explanation.surface: A key scientific law is described as sounding like it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the principal reason or person is the chief, foremost one.

clue.text: Failure of organiser's earliest expedition into space

indicators.note: earliest means just the first letter of the word for organiser

parts.note: a space mission is a journey into space

explanation.surface: The planner's first space trip was a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is a failure to do something, a neglect or oversight.

clue.text: Starts to analyse Mihir Bose's insights into playing in goal

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letter of each of the next four words is taken
playing means the letters of the following word are shuffled about

explanation.surface: Analysing a sports journalist's views about playing in goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Mihir Bose is a British sports journalist. 'playing' rearranges INTO to give TION. 'in' is a link word; goal looks like football, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: an aim or goal one strives for is an ambition.

clue.text: Drink causing fellow a bit of indigestion

parts.note: Martin is a man's name, standing for any fellow

indicators.note: a bit of means only the first letter of the word for stomach trouble is taken

explanation.surface: A drink gives some man a touch of heartburn.
explanation.definitionFit: A martini is a cocktail of gin or vodka and vermouth, an example of an alcoholic drink.

clue.text: Very unpleasant for one cooking with miso

indicators.note: cooking means the letters are stirred up into a new order

explanation.surface: A dish made with miso is foul for one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' and 'with' are link words; 'cooking' rearranges ONE and MISO.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: noisome means offensive or disgusting, especially of a smell.

clue.text: John, for instance, makes this type of music

definitions.meaning: the Book of John is one of the four New Testament accounts of Christ's life
a style of African-American Christian music

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: John is one of the four evangelists' books, and the word also names a religious music genre.

clue.text: A small amount of it gives off heat

definitions.meaning: a trace, as in an ... of truth
the heating part in a kettle or oven

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses: a small trace of something, and the electric heating coil in an appliance.

clue.text: Extremely distressing for soldier trapped in overturned vehicle

indicators.note: trapped in means the soldier is held inside the vehicle word
overturned means the vehicle word is read backwards

parts.note: a cart is a vehicle
a GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier caught under a flipped vehicle is a terrible sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonyms: a tragic event is calamitous, deeply upsetting.

clue.text: Brought about by misguided pride in son at first

indicators.note: misguided means the letters are led astray into a new order
at first means only the opening letter of the word for son is used

explanation.surface: Something caused by a parent's mistaken pride in their son.
explanation.definitionFit: An act inspired by something was prompted or brought about by it.

clue.text: Fish-monger's back to intervene in quarrel

indicators.note: to intervene in means that letter goes inside the word for quarrel

parts.note: a spat is a petty quarrel

indicators.note: back means the final letter of the word for trader is taken

explanation.surface: A fishmonger turns back to break up an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphen is a trick: Fish is the definition, and monger's back gives R.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprat is a small sea fish of the herring family, an example of a fish.

clue.text: Is involved in plan for getting pirate out of nick

indicators.note: involved in means the word is is put inside the word for plan

parts.note: a map is a plan of an area
pro means for, in favour of

indicators.note: out means the letters of the word for buccaneer are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone is part of a scheme to spring a pirate from jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Nick looks like a prison (British slang), but it is the verb to steal. 'out' rearranges PIRATE into PRIATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To nick is British slang for steal, and to embezzle or take dishonestly is a synonym.

clue.text: Against dismissing current social worker

indicators.note: dismissing means the current symbol is removed from the word for against

parts.note: anti means against
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Someone opposes sacking a present-day social worker.
explanation.walkthrough: Social worker looks like a care professional, but it is an insect living in a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Ants live in organised colonies with worker castes, so the insect is a social worker.

clue.text: Shakespearean standard-bearer's first to be found in river near the centre of Ely

indicators.note: near means the centre letter comes next to the river piece
to be found in means the word for first goes inside the river name

parts.note: the Po is a river in Italy
first is written 1ST, with the figure 1 looking like the letter I

indicators.note: the centre of means the middle letter of the place name

explanation.surface: A flag-carrier in Shakespeare is first seen in a river near Ely Cathedral.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after standard-bearer stands for 'has', a link word. Ely is a cathedral city in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Pistol is Falstaff's swaggering companion in Henry V, who serves as an ancient, an old word for ensign or flag-carrier.

clue.text: A request from Egypt's leader to discuss residing in New York

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the country name
residing in means the word for discuss sits inside the New York abbreviation

parts.note: to treat a subject is to discuss it

explanation.surface: An Egyptian president asks to hold talks while staying in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea, a synonym of request.
